state.methods: Eligible adults with moderate plaque psoriasis were randomized 2:1 to oral ravelimod 20 mg daily or matching placebo for 16 weeks. Tablets were manufactured to be identical in size, colour and taste. Participants, site investigators and the PASI assessors were blinded to treatment allocation until database lock. The randomization list was generated by an independent statistician using permuted blocks of 6.

why: Participants, investigators and PASI assessors are all stated as blinded.

state.methods: This was a multicentre, open-label, randomised trial comparing early laparoscopic cholecystectomy (within 72 h of admission) with delayed surgery after 6-8 weeks in patients with acute calculous cholecystitis. Neither patients, surgeons nor ward staff were masked to allocation. The primary outcome was total length of hospital stay, extracted from the hospital administrative system.

why: Explicitly open-label; nobody masked.

state.methods: Patients were randomly allocated (computer-generated sequence, sealed opaque envelopes) to receive either arthroscopic partial meniscectomy followed by physiotherapy or a 12-week exercise therapy programme alone. Outcomes (KOOS, one-leg hop test) were collected at 3, 12 and 24 months by a physiotherapist who was unaware of group allocation and who was not involved in delivering either intervention. Patients were instructed not to reveal their treatment to the assessor.

why: Only the assessing physiotherapist was blinded; surgery vs exercise cannot be hidden from patients.

state.methods: Twenty-four healthy male volunteers completed two experimental trials separated by 7 days, ingesting either 6 mg/kg caffeine or a placebo (maltodextrin) in opaque gelatin capsules 60 min before a 20-km cycling time trial. Participants were not told which capsule they received. The researchers supervising the time trials knew the order of conditions, as they were also responsible for preparing the capsules.

why: Participants unaware; supervising researchers knew the conditions.

state.methods: We conducted a placebo-controlled trial of vitamin D3 (4000 IU/day) versus placebo in 312 older adults with a history of falls. Randomization was stratified by site and baseline 25(OH)D level. The primary outcome was the rate of falls over 12 months, recorded with monthly falls calendars returned by post. Secondary outcomes included gait speed and handgrip strength, measured at baseline and month 12.

why: Placebo-controlled, but the excerpt never states that anyone was blinded.

state.methods: A double-blind, placebo-controlled design was used. Participants received either 300 mg of the study compound or placebo in identical capsules twice daily for eight weeks. The primary endpoint was change in HAM-D17 total score from baseline to week 8.

why: Bare 'double-blind' with matched placebo capsules is read as participants plus investigators/assessors blinded (rule applied throughout).

state.methods: Mice (C57BL/6J, 8-10 weeks old, n = 12 per group) were randomly assigned to receive intraperitoneal injections of compound K-17 (10 mg/kg) or vehicle daily for 14 days. Behavioural testing (open field, elevated plus maze) was video-recorded and scored by an experimenter blinded to treatment group using coded file names. Tissue collection and western blots were performed by the same investigator who dosed the animals, without blinding.

why: Only the behavioural scorer was blinded; animals are not blinded participants.

state.methods: Thirty-two primary schools in the Western Cape were randomised to deliver the 'Read Together' paired-reading programme or continue usual literacy teaching. Because the intervention involved visible changes to the timetable, teachers, pupils and parents were aware of their school's allocation, and the fieldworkers administering the end-of-year reading test were not masked either.

why: States teachers, pupils, parents and testers were all unmasked.

state.methods: Participants with chronic neck pain were randomised to eight sessions of true acupuncture or sham acupuncture using non-penetrating Streitberger needles at non-acupoints. Participants were blinded to group assignment; the success of blinding was checked at week 4 by asking participants to guess their allocation. The acupuncturists could not be blinded. Pain intensity (VAS) and the Neck Disability Index were self-reported by participants via an online form.

why: Only participants blinded; acupuncturists not, and no separate assessor was masked (self-report does not add assessor blinding).

state.methods: Data from 1,204 consecutive patients undergoing elective hip arthroplasty were collected prospectively. Patients were randomised by the hospital pharmacy to tranexamic acid 1 g IV at induction or no tranexamic acid. Blood loss was calculated with the Gross formula from pre- and postoperative haemoglobin. Transfusion decisions followed a restrictive protocol (Hb < 80 g/L).

why: No statement about blinding or masking anywhere.

state.methods: PROBE design (prospective, randomised, open, blinded end-point). Patients with atrial fibrillation after ablation were assigned to continue apixaban or stop anticoagulation at 3 months. Patients and treating physicians knew the allocation. All suspected strokes, systemic emboli and bleeding events were adjudicated by an independent clinical events committee unaware of treatment assignment.

why: The word 'open' appears, but endpoint adjudicators were blinded, so assessors only.

state.methods: Adolescents (13-17 y) with a DSM-5 diagnosis of social anxiety disorder were randomised to 14 weekly sessions of group CBT or a waitlist. Diagnostic status at post-treatment was established with the ADIS-5 interview conducted by clinicians who were blind to condition and had no contact with the treatment groups. Adolescents and their parents obviously knew whether they had started therapy.

why: Interviewing clinicians were blind; families knew their condition.

state.methods: Study design: randomised, triple-blind, placebo-controlled. Participants, care providers, and the statisticians who analysed the data were unaware of group allocation until the analysis was complete. Probiotic sachets (Lactobacillus rhamnosus LR-9, 10^9 CFU) and placebo sachets (maltodextrin) were indistinguishable in appearance, smell and taste.

why: Participants, care providers and analysts all blinded.

state.methods: Open-label extension. All patients who completed the 24-week double-blind period of TRIAL-A were eligible to receive active drug (vodatinib 50 mg) for a further 48 weeks. Efficacy and safety assessments continued at 12-week intervals.

why: The excerpt describes the open-label extension period; the earlier double-blind phase is a different study period.

state.methods: Participants were told they would be testing 'two different brands' of sports drink; in fact, one contained 6% carbohydrate and the other was an artificially sweetened, taste-matched placebo. The order was counterbalanced. Performance on the Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 was recorded by coaches who prepared the drinks.

why: Participants deceived about content (blinded); coaches who recorded outcomes prepared the drinks and so knew.

state.methods: Three hundred source sentences were translated by our system and by two baselines. Outputs were shuffled and presented side by side to five professional translators, who rated adequacy and fluency on a 1-5 scale. Raters were not told which system produced which output, and the position of each system's output was randomised per item.

why: Only raters were blinded to system identity; there are no participants receiving an intervention.

state.methods: We recruited 88 women with stress urinary incontinence from two urogynaecology clinics in Lyon and Grenoble. After baseline assessment, women were allocated by minimisation (age, BMI, parity) to supervised pelvic floor muscle training or written instructions only. The pad test and ICIQ-UI SF were repeated at 3 months. Analysis followed the intention-to-treat principle.

why: Allocation described, but no word on blinding.

state.methods: Masking: none. This was an open-label study; both the investigators and participants were aware of the treatment assigned (subcutaneous semaglutide vs. dietary counselling alone). HbA1c was measured by a central laboratory.

why: 'Masking: none' and open-label stated.

state.methods: Rats underwent unilateral sciatic nerve crush and were randomised to daily low-level laser therapy or sham irradiation (device switched on, emitter covered). The investigator performing the walking-track analysis and the histomorphometry was blinded to group; codes were broken only after all measurements were entered.

why: Only the investigator doing outcome measurements was blinded; animals are not blinded participants.

state.methods: Single-blind, randomised, sham-controlled trial. Patients with knee osteoarthritis received either real transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) or sham TENS through an identical-looking unit that emitted a light and sound but no current after 30 seconds. The physiotherapist applying the units was aware of allocation and also recorded the WOMAC scores at follow-up visits.

why: 'Single-blind' with a sham device; the physiotherapist who recorded outcomes knew allocation, so only patients blinded.

state.methods: Children aged 6-12 with ADHD were randomised to a 10-week omega-3 fatty acid supplement or olive oil placebo capsules. Parents, children, teachers and the research psychologists administering the Conners' rating scales were kept unaware of treatment group throughout. The trial pharmacist held the code.

why: Children/parents and rating psychologists all blinded.

state.methods: Allocation concealment was ensured by central web-based randomisation (Sealed Envelope Ltd); the sequence was not accessible to recruiting staff. Patients were then assigned to either early mobilisation (within 24 h) or standard care after hip fracture surgery. The primary outcome was independent walking at discharge.

why: Allocation concealment is described, which is not blinding; blinding itself is never mentioned.

state.methods: Given the nature of the interventions (mindfulness course vs. an active control involving group light exercise), it was not possible to blind participants or facilitators. Outcome data were collected with self-report questionnaires completed online. No attempt was made to blind the data analyst.

why: Participants, facilitators and analyst all stated unblinded, so nobody blinded even though 'open-label' is not used.

state.methods: Sections of an introductory statistics course (n = 6 sections, 412 students) were randomly assigned to weekly retrieval-practice quizzes or weekly re-reading assignments. The final exam was common to all sections and graded by teaching assistants from other courses who did not know which section a script came from. Students were aware of their section's activities but were not told about the study hypothesis.

why: Graders were blinded; students knew their activity (not knowing the hypothesis is not blinding to assignment).

state.methods: Patients undergoing elective third-molar extraction under local anaesthesia were randomly given preoperative ibuprofen 400 mg or an identical placebo tablet by a nurse not otherwise involved in the study. The patient and the oral surgeon, who also recorded postoperative pain and swelling, did not know which tablet had been taken.

why: Patient and the surgeon-assessor were both unaware.

state.methods: 2.3 Blinding. Participants were blinded to whether they received active or placebo nasal spray (both delivered in identical 10 mL amber bottles with the same saline vehicle). Study nurses who dispensed sprays and collected symptom diaries were unblinded because they also managed the rescue-medication log. Nasal symptom scores were entered by participants themselves.

why: Participants blinded; study nurses explicitly unblinded.

state.methods: Patients with newly diagnosed multiple myeloma ineligible for transplant were randomised to daratumumab-lenalidomide-dexamethasone or lenalidomide-dexamethasone. The trial was open label. Response was assessed per IMWG criteria using a validated computer algorithm.

why: States the trial was open label.

state.methods: Forty-two recreationally trained men performed 8 weeks of resistance training (3x/week) and were randomised to creatine monohydrate 5 g/d or placebo. Body composition was measured by DXA at weeks 0 and 8; 1RM bench press and squat were tested by the lead investigator. Supplement compliance was checked with sachet counts.

why: Placebo arm exists but blinding is never stated for anyone.

state.methods: Study participants and investigators were blinded to group allocation (double-blind). Active treatment consisted of dapagliflozin 10 mg; placebo tablets were identical in appearance. Blinding was maintained until all participants completed the week 52 visit.

why: Participants and investigators explicitly blinded.

state.methods: Men undergoing elective unilateral inguinal hernia repair were randomised in theatre to Lichtenstein open repair or TEP laparoscopic repair. Dressings of identical size were applied over the groin and all port sites in both groups so that the research nurse assessing pain and chronic groin discomfort at 1 week and 6 months could not tell which procedure had been performed. Patients were informed of their procedure at discharge.

why: Identical dressings masked the assessing nurse; patients told their procedure.

state.methods: Pacientes adultos con lumbalgia crónica fueron aleatorizados a manipulación espinal o manipulación simulada. The sham procedure used a low-velocity positioning without thrust. Patients were not informed which technique they received. The chiropractors delivering treatment were necessarily aware of allocation; the outcome assessor (Oswestry Disability Index, administered in person) was a separate clinician kept unaware of group.

why: Patients and a separate outcome assessor were blinded; only chiropractors knew.

state.methods: Neither the participants nor the research team were blinded. Participants chose a convenient date for the first session and were then allocated, in order of enrolment, to the high-intensity interval training or moderate continuous training arm.

why: Explicitly neither participants nor team blinded.

state.methods: We recruited 36 professional developers who each completed four programming tasks in a VS Code instance with an autocomplete plugin. For two tasks the plugin was backed by our model and for two by the baseline; the plugin UI was identical and participants were told only that they were testing 'an autocomplete tool'. Task completion time was logged automatically; correctness was judged by two of the authors who knew the condition for each session.

why: Developers didn't know which model; the authors judging correctness knew condition.

state.methods: Histological sections were coded by a technician and examined by two pathologists blinded to group assignment. Fibrosis was quantified with Sirius red staining (percentage area) in 10 random fields per section. Sheep had been randomised to receive the decellularised scaffold or no scaffold at the time of tendon repair.

why: Pathologists (assessors) blinded; animals and surgeons not relevant/not blinded.

state.methods: Participants were randomised to receive either the Mediterranean-diet intervention (dietitian-led cooking classes plus weekly provision of extra-virgin olive oil) or a low-fat control diet. Anthropometric and blood pressure measurements were obtained at baseline, 6 and 12 months following standard operating procedures. Fasting blood samples were stored at -80 °C.

why: Nothing about blinding or masking.

state.methods: Veterans with PTSD were randomised to prolonged exposure or present-centred therapy. Both treatments were presented to veterans as 'active trauma-focused treatments'. CAPS-5 interviews were conducted by independent evaluators masked to treatment condition; evaluators' guesses were recorded after each interview to check masking. Veterans were aware of which therapy they received.

why: Veterans knew their therapy (presenting both as active is not blinding); only evaluators masked.

state.methods: The study was conducted under single-blind conditions: patients were unaware of whether their dressing contained silver. Wound area was traced by the treating nurse at each weekly dressing change.

why: Single-blind specified as patients only; treating nurse traced wounds.

state.methods: Randomised, double-masked, sham-controlled study. Eyes with centre-involving diabetic macular oedema received intravitreal injections of the study drug or sham injection (syringe hub pressed against the conjunctiva). Visual acuity examiners and patients were masked; the injecting ophthalmologist was not.

why: Patients and visual acuity examiners masked.

state.methods: Open-label randomised trial. However, the primary endpoint (progression-free survival) was assessed by blinded independent central review (BICR) of CT and MRI scans according to RECIST 1.1. Investigator-assessed PFS was a secondary endpoint.

why: Labelled open-label, but the primary outcome was assessed by blinded central reviewers.

state.methods: The trial had an open design. All participants received a take-home naloxone kit and were randomly assigned to peer-delivered or pharmacist-delivered overdose training.

why: 'Open design' means nobody was blinded (open label), although the phrase is unusual.

state.methods: We prospectively enrolled 60 patients scheduled for total knee arthroplasty under spinal anaesthesia. Patients were randomly assigned to adductor canal block with 20 mL ropivacaine 0.5% or 20 mL normal saline. Morphine consumption in the first 48 h was recorded from the PCA device. Pain at rest and on movement was measured with an NRS at 6, 12, 24 and 48 h.

why: Saline control implies blinding could have been done, but the excerpt does not say anyone was blinded.

state.methods: Third-year medical students were randomised to learn ECG interpretation through a spaced-repetition app or through standard lectures. Students were aware of their allocation. The ECG interpretation test was scored by two cardiologists; the scoring was performed on anonymised answer sheets, and the cardiologists did not know which teaching method each student had received.

why: Students knew; cardiologist scorers blinded.

state.methods: Study drug and placebo were provided as identical oral solutions in numbered bottles, prepared by the hospital pharmacy according to a computer-generated list. Only the pharmacy held the allocation list. Children, parents, attending physicians and research nurses measuring the croup score were unaware of the allocation.

why: Children/parents and croup-score nurses unaware.

state.methods: Blinding of participants was achieved using sham laser (device switched on but without emission; both produced an identical beep). Outcome measures (pain VAS and grip strength) were recorded by the same therapist who applied the laser, who knew which mode was active.

why: Participants blinded by sham; therapist-assessor knew.

state.methods: Consecutive patients presenting with first-episode psychosis to three early intervention services in Birmingham were followed up for 2 years. Exposure to cannabis was assessed using the Cannabis Experience Questionnaire at baseline. Relapse was defined as readmission or a 25% increase in PANSS positive score.

why: Observational cohort; blinding not mentioned at all.

state.methods: This is an unblinded trial. Allocation was by the trial office after consent; the participant and the recruiting GP were then told the group by telephone.

why: Explicitly unblinded.

state.methods: Zebrafish larvae (5 dpf) were exposed to 0, 1 or 10 µM bisphenol S in 24-well plates. Locomotor activity was tracked automatically (DanioVision). Plates were labelled with letter codes by a lab member not involved in the analysis, so that the person running the tracking and exporting the movement data was unaware of the exposure concentration.

why: The person running and analysing the tracking was blinded via coded plates; larvae aren't blinded participants.

state.methods: Patients received either the neuromodulation device or an identical sham device in random order, each for 8 weeks with a 4-week washout. The sham device vibrated and displayed the same lights but delivered no stimulation. Patients were blinded. Headache days were recorded by patients in an electronic diary; the diary data were analysed by the sponsor's statistician, who had access to the treatment codes.

why: Patients blinded; the analysing statistician had the codes, so assessor/analyst not blinded.

state.methods: Randomisation was carried out using a random number table. The acupuncturist opened the envelope immediately before the first session. The intervention group received manual acupuncture at LI4, ST36 and SP6; the control group received usual care. Outcomes were measured at 4 and 12 weeks.

why: Envelope opening described, but no blinding statement.

state.methods: All volunteers, the clinical staff administering the vaccine and those assessing reactogenicity and immunogenicity endpoints were blinded. Vaccine and placebo (saline) syringes were prepared by unblinded pharmacists and masked with opaque labels before handover.

why: Volunteers and endpoint assessors blinded.

state.methods: Study design and participants. RESOLVE-HF was a randomised, placebo-controlled trial conducted at 94 sites in 11 countries (Poland, Hungary, Brazil, Argentina, South Africa, India, Japan, Canada, Germany, Spain and the UK). Adults aged 40 years or older with chronic heart failure (NYHA class II-IV) and LVEF of 40% or less were eligible if they had an NT-proBNP concentration of at least 600 pg/mL. Randomisation and masking. Participants were randomly assigned (1:1) via an interactive web response system to oral tolvastrin 5 mg once daily or matching placebo, stratified by region and diabetes status. Participants, investigators, site staff, the sponsor's study team and the clinical endpoint committee were masked to treatment assignment. An independent data monitoring committee reviewed unblinded data at prespecified intervals. Procedures. Study visits occurred at weeks 2, 4, 16 and every 16 weeks thereafter. At each visit, vital signs, NYHA class and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire were recorded, and blood was drawn for central laboratory analysis of NT-proBNP, potassium and creatinine.

why: Participants, investigators and the endpoint committee were masked.

state.methods: Methods: 60 pts w/ chronic plantar fasciitis randomised (sealed envelopes) to ESWT 3 sessions vs corticosteroid inj x1. no blinding (pts + treating Dr aware). FFI + VAS at 6wk, 3mo, 6mo by treating Dr.

why: 'no blinding (pts + treating Dr aware)'.

state.methods: Study design: A prospective, randomized, controlled trial was conducted at a tertiary hospital in Riyadh between January 2022 and March 2023. Women undergoing elective caesarean section under spinal anaesthesia were allocated to prophylactic phenylephrine infusion or rescue boluses of ephedrine. Maternal blood pressure was recorded every minute until delivery by an automated monitor. Umbilical arterial blood gas was analysed immediately after delivery. The incidence of nausea and vomiting was recorded by the anaesthetist in charge.

why: Design and outcomes described; blinding never mentioned.

state.methods: Patients with frozen shoulder were randomised to hydrodilatation plus physiotherapy or physiotherapy alone. It was not feasible to blind patients or the treating physiotherapists. However, shoulder range of motion and the Shoulder Pain and Disability Index were measured by an independent assessor who was blinded to allocation. The success of assessor blinding was evaluated at the final visit: the assessor guessed allocation correctly in 54% of cases.

why: Patients and physios unblinded; independent assessor blinded.

state.methods: In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover design, 14 trained rowers completed a 2000-m ergometer time trial after ingesting sodium bicarbonate (0.3 g/kg) or sodium chloride placebo (0.045 g/kg) in gelatin capsules. The two supplements were prepared by an independent researcher who did not take part in data collection; the researchers conducting the trials and the rowers were therefore unaware of the condition. Blood pH and bicarbonate were measured with a blood gas analyser before and after exercise.

why: Rowers and trial-conducting researchers unaware.

state.methods: The subjects were not informed of their group assignment and received either an active or inactive (placebo) kinesio tape application, which looked identical but applied with no tension. The investigator who applied the tape also performed the outcome measurements (active knee flexion range and pressure pain threshold).

why: Subjects blinded; the investigator measuring outcomes applied the tape, so knew.

state.methods: We randomly assigned 1,850 patients with stable coronary artery disease to percutaneous coronary intervention plus optimal medical therapy or optimal medical therapy alone. The trial was open-label; however, all clinical events were adjudicated by a committee whose members were unaware of the treatment assignments.

why: Open-label for patients/clinicians, but events adjudicated by a blinded committee.

state.methods: Twenty patients with treatment-resistant depression were randomised to ketamine infusion or midazolam infusion. As this was an open-label pilot, the psychiatrists rating the MADRS were aware of the infusion given, and patients were informed of their allocation after the first infusion.

why: Open-label; raters and patients aware.

state.methods: Study population and interventions: Premature infants (<32 weeks' gestation) admitted to the NICU at Hospital Universitario Del Valle were randomised to receive probiotic drops or no supplementation. Necrotising enterocolitis (Bell stage ≥ II) was diagnosed by the attending neonatologist. Weight gain was recorded daily by nursing staff. Randomisation used a computerised block sequence and allocation was concealed from recruiting staff until the moment of assignment.

why: Mentions concealment of allocation before assignment, not blinding after; no blinding statement.

state.methods: Human evaluation. We asked crowdworkers on a platform to compare pairs of summaries for the same article, choosing which was more faithful. Each pair contained one summary from our system and one from the strongest baseline. We did not reveal system names to annotators, and the left/right order was randomised. The final win rates were computed by the first author.

why: Annotators (the assessors) were blinded to system; no intervention participants.

state.methods: Blinding: Participants were blinded to whether they received verum or placebo homeopathic globules (both prepared by a pharmacy in identical vials). The homeopathic physicians conducting follow-up consultations and completing the physician-rated outcome forms were also blinded, as the vials were numbered only.

why: Participants and physician-raters blinded.

state.methods: Participants were randomized to 12 weeks of daily cocoa flavanol extract (500 mg) or placebo. Cognitive testing (Modified Benton Task, list learning) was performed at baseline and week 12 in a quiet room.

why: Placebo mentioned, blinding not.

state.methods: Single-blind trial (outcome assessor). Adults after first-ever stroke were allocated to robot-assisted gait training or conventional overground gait training, 5 days per week for 4 weeks. The 6-minute walk test and Functional Ambulation Category were recorded by a therapist blinded to allocation.

why: Single-blind explicitly refers to the outcome assessor.

state.methods: Participants were randomised to internet-delivered CBT for insomnia or to an online sleep hygiene education programme. Both conditions were described to participants as 'sleep improvement programmes' and were visually similar; participants were not told which was the experimental condition. Outcomes (Insomnia Severity Index, sleep diary) were collected automatically on the web platform. The research team monitoring the platform was aware of group allocation.

why: Participants kept unaware which programme was experimental (blinded); research team aware and outcomes self-reported.

state.methods: Open-label, randomised, active-controlled, non-inferiority study. Patients with uncomplicated urinary tract infection received fosfomycin 3 g single dose or nitrofurantoin 100 mg twice daily for 5 days. Clinical cure at day 14 was determined by the investigator; microbiological cure by the central laboratory.

why: Explicitly open-label; no blinded assessment described.

state.methods: Dogs with naturally occurring osteoarthritis (client-owned) were randomised to receive an anti-NGF monoclonal antibody or saline injection monthly for three months. Owners, who completed the Canine Brief Pain Inventory, and the veterinarians performing orthopaedic examinations were unaware of treatment. Injections were prepared by a pharmacist.

why: Owners (proxy participants/reporters) and examining vets blinded; treat owner blinding as participant-side blinding.

state.methods: Students in grade 8 at 18 schools in Nairobi County were randomly assigned at the class level to a tablet-based adaptive maths programme or standard instruction. Endline maths assessments were administered by enumerators hired by a survey firm; these enumerators were not informed of which classes were in the treatment group. Teachers and students, of course, knew whether they were using tablets.

why: Enumerators uninformed; teachers and students knew.

state.methods: Patients were randomised to receive 5 ml of 0.25% bupivacaine or 5 ml normal saline infiltrated at the port sites at the end of laparoscopic cholecystectomy. The anaesthetist who prepared the syringe was not involved in postoperative care. The patient was blinded to group allocation. Postoperative pain scores were recorded by the operating surgeon, who performed the infiltration from an unlabelled syringe.

why: Patient blinded, and the surgeon-assessor used an unlabelled syringe so was also unaware (no explicit 'blinded' for surgeon).

state.methods: The trial was single-blinded; patients did not know whether their knee injection contained platelet-rich plasma or hyaluronic acid, as a screen blocked their view of the syringe. The orthopaedic surgeon who injected also assessed WOMAC at follow-up.

why: Patients blinded via screen; the injecting surgeon assessed outcomes.

state.methods: Electronic health records of 14,322 adults who started either a DPP-4 inhibitor or a sulfonylurea as second-line therapy between 2015 and 2020 were retrieved from the regional database. Propensity score matching (1:1, caliper 0.05) was used to balance baseline covariates. Outcomes were identified by ICD-10 codes.

why: Observational database study; no blinding mentioned.

state.methods: Blinding was not possible for participants or therapists due to the nature of the interventions (aquatic therapy vs land-based exercise). Outcome assessors were not blinded either, because the same research physiotherapist conducted all assessments for logistical reasons.

why: Participants, therapists and assessors all unblinded.

state.methods: All statistical analyses were performed by a statistician blinded to group allocation (groups were labelled A and B in the dataset). Patients were randomised to surgical fixation or cast immobilisation for undisplaced scaphoid waist fractures.

why: Only the analyst was blinded; patients obviously know surgery vs cast.

state.methods: Double-blind. Participants were given either the herbal tea blend (chamomile, lemon balm, valerian) or a flavour-matched tea without active herbs in identical sachets.

why: Bare 'double-blind' with matched sachets; read as participants plus investigators/assessors per the double-blind rule.

state.methods: Participants (N = 160 undergraduates) were randomly assigned to receive either a 200 mg caffeine tablet or a placebo tablet before completing a sustained attention task. Participants were not told which tablet they had received. The experimenter who handed out the tablets and ran the session was aware of condition. Reaction times were recorded by software.

why: Participants unaware; experimenter aware.

state.methods: We performed a randomised trial of a structured smoking cessation counselling programme delivered by pharmacists versus brief advice. Abstinence at 6 months was biochemically verified by exhaled CO < 10 ppm. Participants received a £10 voucher for attending follow-up.

why: No blinding statement.

state.methods: Participants were randomised to receive 12 sessions of either real or sham repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) over the left DLPFC. The sham coil looked and sounded identical to the active coil. Participants were blinded to condition. The rTMS operator was not blinded. Depression severity was rated with the HAM-D by the same psychiatrist who prescribed the stimulation parameters and reviewed session logs.

why: Participants blinded; operator and prescribing psychiatrist-rater were not.

state.methods: Design: pragmatic, open-label, randomised trial embedded in routine care in 23 Danish general practices. Patients with uncomplicated hypertension were randomised to home blood pressure telemonitoring with pharmacist-led titration, or usual care. No participants, clinicians or data collectors were masked, and outcomes were taken from the practice records.

why: Open-label; nobody masked.

state.methods:
Methods — Blinding
Participants: blinded (identical placebo inhaler)
Investigators: unblinded (site pharmacist also acted as sub-investigator)
Outcome assessment: FEV1 by site spirometry technicians, unblinded
Data analysis: unblinded

why: Participants blinded; investigators, spirometry and analysis unblinded.

state.methods: Open-label. Because both regimens (weekly carboplatin-paclitaxel vs three-weekly) differed in schedule, no attempt at masking patients or treating oncologists was made. Tumour response was assessed by the treating oncologist using RECIST 1.1 on local imaging.

why: Open-label, and response assessed by the unmasked treating oncologist.

state.methods: Women undergoing IVF were randomly allocated to acupuncture or placebo acupuncture using the Park sham device on the day of embryo transfer. Women were unaware of which needle they received. The acupuncturists were aware of group allocation. Clinical pregnancy was confirmed by ultrasound at 6-7 weeks by fertility clinic staff who were not informed about the trial.

why: Women blinded, and the ultrasound staff (assessors) were unaware because they were not told of the trial.

state.methods: Participants with irritable bowel syndrome received either the low-FODMAP diet or a sham diet designed to look similarly restrictive (excluding foods not high in FODMAPs). Participants were blinded to which diet was the 'active' one; dietitians delivering the diets were aware. IBS-SSS scores were collected by participants via a questionnaire returned to the dietitian.

why: Participants blinded via sham diet; dietitians aware.

state.methods: Assignment to the two arms (bariatric surgery vs intensive medical therapy) was made by a central telephone service. The HbA1c primary endpoint was measured by a central laboratory. Quality of life was assessed with the SF-36.

why: A central lab measured the endpoint, but no blinding of any group is stated.

state.methods: We ran a within-subjects study with 24 radiologists reading 120 chest radiographs each, once with AI decision support and once without (4-week washout, order randomised). Radiologists necessarily knew when AI support was displayed. Ground-truth labels were established by a panel of three thoracic radiologists who did not participate as readers and were unaware of which reads were AI-assisted; they only saw the images and the CT reports.

why: Readers knew the AI condition; only the ground-truth panel was blinded.

state.methods: Children with acute otitis media were assigned to amoxicillin or placebo suspension, taste- and colour-matched. Children, parents and study physicians who performed otoscopic assessments were unaware of assignment. Unblinding was allowed for clinical deterioration.

why: Children/parents and otoscopy physicians unaware.

state.methods: The study was a randomised, parallel-group trial comparing two cognitive rehabilitation programmes in adults with mild traumatic brain injury. Participants attended 10 weekly group sessions. Neuropsychological assessments at baseline and 12 weeks were administered by trained research assistants.

why: No mention of masking of anyone.

state.methods: Participants were blinded to the hypothesis but not to their group: those in the standing-desk arm received a sit-stand workstation while controls kept their usual desk. Physical activity was measured with thigh-worn accelerometers and processed with automated software. Research staff were not blinded.

why: Blinding to hypothesis isn't blinding to assignment; participants and staff knew groups, so nobody blinded.

state.methods: Patients with alcohol use disorder received naltrexone 50 mg or placebo daily for 12 weeks in a double-blind fashion. Heavy drinking days were assessed with the timeline followback method administered by research staff.

why: Bare 'double-blind' with placebo; treated as participants plus investigators/assessors per rule.

state.methods: Fish oil (2 g EPA+DHA/day) or corn oil placebo was provided in soft-gel capsules. Capsules had a slight fish odour in both groups to maintain participant blinding. Investigators measuring triglycerides and blood pressure were not blinded because the capsule bottles were labelled with group colour codes known to staff.

why: Participant blinding maintained; investigators not blinded.

state.methods: Rats were assigned by a random number generator to a high-fat diet with or without resveratrol supplementation. Glucose tolerance tests were performed at week 10. Liver tissue was fixed in formalin and steatosis graded by a pathologist.

why: No blinding statement for the pathologist or anyone.

state.methods: Patients with bilateral age-related cataract had one eye randomised to femtosecond laser-assisted cataract surgery and the other to conventional phacoemulsification. Patients were not told which eye received which procedure, and the postoperative examiner measuring endothelial cell density and corrected distance visual acuity was also masked. The surgeon obviously was not.

why: Patients and examiner masked; only the surgeon knew.

state.methods: This study is open label. Hospitalised adults with community-acquired pneumonia were randomised to 3 or 8 days of beta-lactam therapy. Clinical cure at day 15 was determined by an independent physician who was unaware of treatment duration.

why: Called open label, but the day-15 cure assessor was unaware of allocation.

state.methods: Participants were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to one of three conditions: an expressive writing task about a stressful event, a positive writing task, or a neutral writing task about daily activities. Instructions were delivered on a computer screen. Participants were told the study was about 'writing and wellbeing'. Mood (PANAS) and physical symptoms were self-reported at 1 and 4 weeks.

why: A cover story is described, but no one is stated as blinded to assignment; the task itself reveals the condition.

state.methods: Participants with chronic low back pain were randomised to a 6-week yoga course or to a self-care book. Participants and instructors were aware of allocation. Follow-up questionnaires (Roland-Morris, pain bothersomeness) were mailed back to the study office and scored by a research assistant who was blinded to group.

why: Participants and instructors aware; only the scoring research assistant blinded.

state.methods: Masking: participants only. Players were told they would receive one of two 'recovery compression garments' but half received garments with graduated compression and half received a size-matched garment with no compression. The strength and conditioning coaches who ran the countermovement jump testing handed out the garments and knew which was which.

why: Masking stated as participants only; coaches knew.

state.methods: Neither patients nor physicians were blinded to treatment allocation. Patients with stage 3 chronic kidney disease were randomised to a very-low-protein diet supplemented with ketoanalogues or a conventional low-protein diet. eGFR was calculated from serum creatinine measured in the hospital laboratory.

why: Neither patients nor physicians blinded; no blinded assessment.

state.methods: To reduce bias, all MRI scans were anonymised and read in random order by two musculoskeletal radiologists who were blinded to the treatment group and to clinical findings. Patients with rotator cuff tears had been randomised to arthroscopic repair or non-operative physiotherapy.

why: Radiologist readers blinded; surgery vs physio can't be hidden from patients.

state.methods: The trial was double-blinded: neither the participant nor the researcher who administered the tDCS and ran the cognitive tests knew whether the stimulation was active or sham. The device was pre-programmed with a code by a technician not otherwise involved.

why: Participant and administering/testing researcher both unaware.

state.methods: Participants were blinded to allocation. Study drug (low-dose naltrexone 4.5 mg) and placebo were compounded in identical capsules. The principal investigator, who conducted all follow-up visits and recorded the FIQR score, held the randomisation list.

why: Participants blinded; the PI who recorded outcomes held the list, so assessor not blinded.

state.methods: In this trial, veterans with knee osteoarthritis received physical therapy either in clinic or via telehealth. The trial is not blinded. WOMAC was collected by telephone by a research coordinator who also scheduled the physical therapy visits.

why: 'The trial is not blinded'; coordinator knew allocation.

state.methods: Pairs of hospital wards were randomised to a nurse-led early warning score escalation protocol or usual practice. The number of unplanned ICU admissions and in-hospital cardiac arrests was extracted from the hospital incident database.

why: Nothing on blinding.

state.methods: Trial design. This was a 12-week, randomised, parallel-group, dose-ranging study conducted at 41 centres in the United States, Mexico and Poland. After a 2-week screening period, patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis (EASI ≥ 16, IGA ≥ 3, BSA ≥ 10%) were randomised 1:1:1:1 to subcutaneous lerokimab 75 mg, 150 mg, 300 mg every 2 weeks, or placebo. To preserve the blind across dose groups, all patients received two injections at each visit using a double-dummy technique; volumes and syringe appearance were identical. Patients, investigators, EASI evaluators and the sponsor's clinical team remained blinded until the final database lock; a separate unblinded pharmacist at each site prepared injections. Topical corticosteroid rescue was permitted after week 4 and recorded as a treatment failure for the primary analysis. Primary endpoint: percent change in EASI from baseline to week 12.

why: Patients, investigators and EASI evaluators all blinded.

state.methods: Owing to the obvious differences between the interventions (cast vs. removable splint for buckle fractures of the distal radius in children), blinding of children, parents and clinicians was not attempted. The primary outcome, PROMIS Upper Extremity score at 3 weeks, was completed by the child with parental help.

why: No blinding attempted for anyone; outcome self-reported.

state.methods: Patients were informed that they would receive one of two 'active' mouthwashes. In reality, the control mouthwash contained no chlorhexidine but was coloured and flavoured identically. Plaque index and gingival index were recorded at baseline, 2 and 4 weeks by the dentist who dispensed the bottles and kept the allocation sheet.

why: Patients unaware of content; dispensing dentist-assessor kept the allocation sheet.

state.methods: Methods: This was a prospective, randomised, comparative study of 80 patients with symptomatic gallstones undergoing laparoscopic cholecystectomy with either three or four ports. Operative time, conversion to open surgery, postoperative pain on a 10-point scale and length of hospital stay were recorded. Cosmetic satisfaction was assessed at 1 month using a patient questionnaire.

why: No statement on blinding.

state.methods: Users of a budgeting app were randomly assigned to receive either a weekly spending summary push notification or no notification. Users were not informed that an experiment was running, per the app's terms of service. Savings balances were extracted from the transaction database by the data science team, who had the assignment table.

why: Users were unaware of the experiment (so unaware of arm assignment); analysts had the assignment table.

state.methods: Open-label, single-arm... correction: two-arm open-label randomised study. Patients received either apixaban or enoxaparin after knee replacement. Venography was read locally by unblinded radiologists.

why: Open-label and venography read by unblinded radiologists.

state.methods: Outcome assessors were blinded. Participants with Parkinson's disease were randomised to a 12-week Argentine tango class or usual activity. MDS-UPDRS part III was scored from video recordings by a movement disorders neurologist blinded to group and time point.

why: Only assessors stated as blinded; dancers know they dance.

state.methods: We compared an oral iron preparation (ferrous bisglycinate 25 mg elemental iron) with a placebo in non-anaemic, iron-deficient female blood donors. Tablets were supplied in identical blister packs. Fatigue was assessed with the FACIT-F questionnaire at 6 and 12 weeks. Ferritin was measured at each visit.

why: Identical packs suggest blinding was intended, but the text never states anyone was blinded.

state.methods: Two hundred and forty Year 10 pupils were randomised within classes to receive written feedback on their essays that either included growth-mindset comments or neutral comments. Pupils did not know that different types of feedback existed. Essays at the second time point were marked by the class teacher, who wrote the feedback and knew each pupil's condition.

why: Pupils unaware of the manipulation; the marking teacher knew conditions.

state.methods: All participants, care providers, outcome assessors and data analysts were blinded to group allocation (quadruple blind). The two melatonin doses (2 mg, 5 mg) and placebo were supplied as identical prolonged-release tablets.

why: Quadruple blind: participants, assessors and analysts.

state.methods: Participants in the treatment arm underwent laparoscopic ovarian drilling; those in the control arm received gonadotropin ovulation induction. As participants and the gynaecologists knew which treatment had been given, the study was considered open. Live birth was the primary outcome, recorded from hospital birth registers.

why: Participants and gynaecologists knew; study considered open.

state.methods: Following middle cerebral artery occlusion, rats were randomised to receive the neuroprotective candidate or vehicle at 2 h. Drug solutions were coded by a colleague so that the surgeon performing the injection, the investigator scoring neurological deficit (Bederson scale) and the person measuring infarct volume from TTC-stained sections were all blinded to treatment.

why: Surgeon and assessors blinded, but animals are not blinded participants, so the fitting option is assessors/investigators only.

state.methods: The patients were blinded to the type of anaesthesia (sevoflurane vs propofol TIVA) because it was administered after induction of unconsciousness; the anaesthetists were not. Quality of recovery (QoR-15) at 24 h was obtained by the attending anaesthetist during the postoperative visit.

why: Patients blinded; attending anaesthetist-assessor aware.

state.methods: Double-blind (participant, investigator). Masking description: The study medication (cannabidiol oral solution 100 mg/mL) and placebo oral solution were identical in appearance and odour. Participants and investigators remained blinded throughout.

why: Participants and investigators blinded.

state.methods: A convenience sample of 120 inpatients was split into two groups based on ward: patients on Ward 7 received hourly rounding and those on Ward 9 received usual nursing care. Falls and call-light use were recorded over 3 months. Patient satisfaction was measured with the HCAHPS instrument at discharge.

why: No blinding stated.

state.methods: Patients were not blinded, as they were fully informed about both treatments (surgical decompression vs. non-surgical rehabilitation) before consent. Clinicians were likewise aware. The self-reported Oswestry Disability Index was the primary outcome.

why: Patients and clinicians not blinded; self-report outcome.

state.methods: Singel blind study. Partisipants were not told weather they got the real or placebo patch. Investigator knew and did the pain scores.
state.study_type: student research report, nicotine patch pilot

why: Participants not told; investigator who scored pain knew.

state.methods: Veterinarians evaluating lameness scores were blinded to treatment. Horses (n = 30) with naturally occurring forelimb lameness were randomly assigned to intra-articular triamcinolone or polyacrylamide hydrogel. Owners were aware of treatment and handled post-injection box rest themselves.

why: Vets scoring lameness blinded; owners aware.

state.methods: Randomised, placebo-controlled trial. 460 adults with acute cough received either the ivy leaf extract syrup or a syrup vehicle. The Leicester Cough Questionnaire was completed at day 7 and 14.

why: Placebo-controlled, but the excerpt never says anyone was blinded.

state.methods: Participants with generalised anxiety disorder were allocated to full CBT or CBT without the worry-exposure component. Both conditions were described to participants as complete treatments and they were not told that a component had been removed. Independent assessors, blind to treatment condition, administered the ADIS-5 and GAD-7 at post-treatment and 6-month follow-up.

why: Participants not told of the removed component (blinded to arm) and assessors blind.

state.methods: Given the nature of the intervention, participants were aware of whether they received the wearable fall-detection device. Outcome data (falls, emergency department visits) were obtained from health records by abstractors who were not blinded to allocation. The analysis was also conducted with knowledge of group allocation.

why: Participants, abstractors and analysts all unblinded; no 'open-label' term but nobody blinded.

state.methods: Allocation: randomised (1:1) by the trial app at the end of the baseline questionnaire. Blinding: none. The app displayed the allocated arm (peer-support chat group vs. self-guided workbook) to the participant immediately, and the study coordinators could see allocation in the dashboard. Outcomes (PHQ-9, GAD-7) were collected in-app.
state.study_type: digital mental health RCT, New Zealand

why: 'Blinding: none'; participants and coordinators saw the allocation.

state.methods: In our preregistered evaluation, native-speaker judges rated the naturalness of speech clips on a 5-point MOS scale. Clips from the three TTS systems and from human recordings were interleaved in random order, and judges were given no information about the source of each clip.

why: Judges (assessors) blind to the source; no participants receiving an intervention.

state.methods: The study was designed as double-blind. Because the active drug frequently produced a characteristic metallic taste, however, the blind was likely compromised for many participants; a blinding questionnaire at week 4 showed 71% correct guesses among participants.

why: Stated double-blind; a likely compromised blind doesn't change who was meant to be blinded.

state.methods: Participants were assigned to groups by coin toss. Participants in the intervention group received daily text-message reminders to take their antiretroviral medication. Adherence was measured by pharmacy refill records and viral load at 12 months.

why: No blinding statement.

state.methods: Masking: Quadruple (Participant, Care Provider, Investigator, Outcomes Assessor). Allocation: Randomized. Intervention Model: Parallel Assignment. Primary Purpose: Treatment.

why: Registry masking lists participant and outcomes assessor.

state.methods: Masking: None (Open Label). Allocation: Randomized. Intervention Model: Parallel Assignment.

why: Registry masking: None (Open Label).

state.methods: Masking: Single (Outcomes Assessor). Allocation: Randomized. Intervention Model: Parallel Assignment. Primary Purpose: Supportive Care.

why: Single masking of the outcomes assessor.

state.methods: Masking: Single (Participant). Allocation: Randomized. Intervention Model: Crossover Assignment. Primary Purpose: Basic Science.

why: Single masking of the participant.

state.methods: Allocation: Randomized. Intervention Model: Parallel Assignment. Primary Purpose: Prevention. Arms: exercise-based fall prevention programme delivered by community physiotherapists vs. an educational booklet. Primary outcome: rate of falls at 12 months (monthly calendars).

why: Registry excerpt omits the masking field entirely.

state.methods: Patients with degenerative meniscal tears were randomised to arthroscopic partial meniscectomy or sham surgery (diagnostic arthroscopy with simulated meniscectomy: the surgeon asked for instruments and used a shaver without blade outside the knee to mimic sound). Patients, the physiotherapists providing postoperative care, and the outcome assessors were unaware of the group assignment. Operating room staff were sworn to secrecy.

why: Patients and outcome assessors blinded via sham surgery.

state.methods: Twenty cyclists completed two 40-km time trials, one while listening to self-selected fast-tempo music and one without music, in randomised order. Heart rate, power output and RPE were recorded every 5 km.

why: Blinding not mentioned (music obviously unblindable, but the text says nothing).

state.methods: Participants received a transdermal patch containing either oestradiol or placebo; neither they nor the gynaecologist performing the follow-up transvaginal ultrasound (endometrial thickness) knew which patch was used. Patches were supplied by the manufacturer in coded packs.

why: Participants and ultrasound-performing gynaecologist unaware.

state.methods: Patients with uncontrolled hypertension were randomised to renal denervation or a sham procedure (renal angiography only). Patients were sedated and wore headphones with music during the procedure so that they could not tell which procedure was performed. The interventional cardiologist performing the procedure was not blinded and was also responsible for the 24-hour ambulatory BP review at 6 months.

why: Patients blinded through sham and sedation; the cardiologist reviewing ABPM was not blinded.

state.methods: Outcome assessment was carried out blind to group: three trained coders rated transcripts of the 10-minute parent-child play sessions using the DPICS-IV, with all identifying information and session dates removed. Families had been randomised to Parent-Child Interaction Therapy or a waitlist.

why: Coders blind; families obviously know if they are in therapy or waitlisted.

state.methods: Mice were housed 4/cage and cages were randomly assigned to treatment. There was no blinding in this study; the same researcher prepared the drinking water, performed the grip strength tests and analysed the data.

why: 'There was no blinding in this study.'

state.methods: Patients were informed of their group after randomisation, as the intervention (a supervised 12-week cardiac rehabilitation programme) could not be concealed. Echocardiography at 12 weeks was performed and interpreted by a sonographer who did not know the patients' allocation; patients were asked not to discuss their rehabilitation with the sonographer.

why: Patients informed; sonographer did not know allocation.

state.methods: Methodology (translated from Portuguese): The study was a randomized clinical trial carried out in the Physiotherapy Clinic of a university in Recife. The volunteers were allocated by drawing lots into two groups: Pilates group (PG) and conventional exercise group (CG). Both groups performed 16 sessions, twice a week. Balance was evaluated with the Berg Balance Scale and the Timed Up and Go test. The evaluations were carried out by the researchers.

why: No blinding mentioned.

state.methods: Participants chatted with two chatbot variants (A: our retrieval-augmented model, B: the base model) for 10 minutes each, order counterbalanced. The variants were presented under neutral names ('Assistant Blue' and 'Assistant Green') and participants were not told how they differed. After each session participants rated helpfulness. Transcripts were then rated for factual accuracy by two annotators who were also shown only the neutral names and were not told which colour corresponded to which model.

why: Both participants and accuracy annotators saw only neutral names.

state.methods: Due to the nature of the intervention, participants could not be blinded. The consultant radiologist who reported bone age on hand X-rays was unaware of whether the child had received growth hormone. The paediatric endocrinologists managing dosing were not blinded.

why: Only the reporting radiologist was blinded.

state.methods: Patients were randomised to receive fixed-dose combination polypill or usual care with separate medications. The trial was open-label. LDL-cholesterol and systolic BP were measured at 12 months by study nurses, who were also aware of allocation.

why: Open-label with aware assessors.

state.methods: Double-blind randomized controlled trial of 1,120 infants. Zinc (10 mg) or placebo was given daily as a dispersible tablet by caregivers.

why: Bare 'double-blind' with placebo tablet; per rule, participants/caregivers plus investigators/assessors.

state.methods: Participants were randomly assigned to receive either a 'high-caffeine' or 'decaffeinated' coffee; in fact both groups received decaf, and only the label differed. Participants were therefore aware of their (sham) group label. Researchers running the arousal measurements also knew the labels.

why: The manipulation is the label itself, which participants and researchers both saw; nobody was blinded to assigned group.

state.methods: Patients with overactive bladder were randomised to percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation or sham stimulation (needle placed with the device set to deliver no current after a brief sensory pulse). Patients were masked to their allocation. Bladder diaries were reviewed and scored by the nurse who performed the stimulation sessions and was aware of allocation.

why: Patients masked; the nurse scoring diaries was aware.

state.methods: Patients undergoing total hip replacement were randomised to the posterior or direct anterior approach. Postoperative radiographs were measured (cup inclination, leg length discrepancy) with software. Functional recovery was measured with the Harris Hip Score at 6 weeks, 3 months and 1 year.

why: No blinding stated.

state.methods: Participants remained blind to whether their hearing aids used the new noise-reduction algorithm or the standard one; the settings were loaded by an audiologist who was not otherwise involved. Speech-in-noise testing was conducted by a second audiologist who also did not know the programme loaded.

why: Participants and testing audiologist unaware.

state.methods: We used a single-blind design in which the students did not know that the online module they took (with or without embedded worked examples) was one of two versions. Exam scripts were marked by the course instructor, who had access to the module logs.

why: Students unaware of versions; the instructor-marker had access to allocation.

state.methods: Guinea pigs were randomly allocated to noise exposure with or without pre-treatment. Auditory brainstem response thresholds were measured by a technician. Cochleae were harvested at day 14, and hair cell counts were performed by an investigator who was masked to the experimental groups.

why: Only the hair cell counter was masked; animals are not blinded participants.

state.methods: The acupuncturist and the patient were aware of the group assignment. An independent assessor who was not aware of the patient's assignment conducted all follow-up interviews by telephone.

why: Acupuncturist and patient aware; only the telephone assessor unaware.

state.methods: Villages were randomised to receive community health worker visits for newborn care or standard services. Neonatal deaths were ascertained by a verbal autopsy team that visited every household with a birth, starting 6 weeks after delivery.
state.notes: verbal autopsy team hired through a separate contract with the district health office

why: A separately hired verbal autopsy team suggests independence, but blinding is not stated.

state.methods: Study design. We did an observer-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled trial at 31 sites in South Africa, Kenya, Peru and the Philippines. Healthy adults aged 18-59 years were randomly assigned (2:1) to two intramuscular doses of the adjuvanted recombinant protein vaccine or saline placebo, 21 days apart. Because the vaccine and placebo differed in appearance, doses were prepared and administered by unblinded pharmacists and vaccinators who had no other role in the trial; syringes were covered with an opaque label. Participants, investigators, site staff responsible for safety follow-up and the laboratory staff running the neutralisation assays were unaware of group assignment. Cases of symptomatic, laboratory-confirmed infection were identified through twice-weekly contact and confirmed by RT-PCR at a central laboratory.

why: Observer-blind: participants, investigators and lab staff unaware; only vaccinators unblinded.

state.methods: Study type: open-label, randomised, controlled, multicentre trial. After randomisation, patients assigned to the intervention group underwent catheter ablation within 4 weeks, whereas the control group continued rate or rhythm control drugs at the discretion of the treating cardiologist. The primary outcome, a composite of death or hospitalisation for worsening heart failure, was reported by site investigators on the eCRF. No central adjudication was performed.

why: Open-label with unblinded site-reported outcomes.

state.methods: Participants swallowed either a gastric balloon capsule or an identical capsule that did not inflate (sham). Participants were blinded until week 16. The endoscopist who checked balloon position at week 4 and the dietitian recording weight were aware of allocation.

why: Participants blinded; endoscopist and weight-recording dietitian aware.

state.methods: The trial was unmasked. Pregnant women at 39 weeks were randomised to induction of labour or expectant management. The primary outcome was caesarean delivery, recorded from the delivery record.

why: 'The trial was unmasked.'

state.methods: Sprinters performed repeated 30-m sprints after 15 min of a dynamic warm-up with or without a 'priming' weighted-vest protocol. Sprint times were measured with timing gates (Brower, automatic). The study was conducted in two sessions at the same time of day, 72 h apart.

why: No blinding stated.

state.methods: Patients were not aware of their treatment allocation, because the control group received topical anaesthetic cream while the intervention group received the same cream plus a vapocoolant spray applied behind a drape. The phlebotomist who did the cannulation and asked patients for their pain score was, however, aware of allocation.

why: Patients unaware via drape; the phlebotomist who asked pain scores knew.

state.methods: Open, randomised trial. Treatment allocation (nurse-led asthma education sessions plus a written action plan vs. usual clinic care) was not concealed from participants, physicians, or those collecting data.

why: Open trial; not concealed from anyone listed.

state.methods: Blinding: Patients were blinded to group allocation as all received the same number of tablets (active drug + placebo, or two placebos, i.e. double-dummy). Outcome data were collected by the treating rheumatologists, who were not blinded because they needed to monitor liver function tests and adjust methotrexate dose.

why: Patients blinded via double-dummy; rheumatologists collecting outcomes not blinded.

state.methods: People with rheumatoid arthritis were randomised to a joint protection education programme or standard information leaflets. Grip strength was measured by an occupational therapist; hand pain and function were rated by participants on the AUSCAN. Measurements were taken in a room separate from the treatment area.

why: Separate room is not a blinding statement; nobody is said to be blinded.

state.methods: Surgical site infection at 30 days was diagnosed by trained wound assessors who were blinded to the type of skin closure (staples vs. subcuticular suture) — staples were removed on day 10 in all patients before the assessment and a standard dressing was applied. Patients were told which closure they had received.

why: Wound assessors blinded; patients told.

state.methods: Participants and outcome assessors were blinded to group allocation. Participants in both groups received identical-appearing sessions on the same software; the active group trained working memory at adaptive difficulty while the control group completed the same tasks at a fixed, low difficulty.

why: Participants and outcome assessors blinded.

state.methods: Since the study was of an intervention delivered to families at home by visiting nurses, it was impossible to blind families or nurses, and since outcome data were collected by the same nurses during their visits, outcome assessment was not blinded either.

why: Families, nurses and outcome collection all unblinded.

state.methods: We conducted a between-subjects online study with 600 participants recruited via a panel provider. Participants were randomly assigned to receive movie recommendations from either our diversity-aware algorithm or a popularity-based baseline. Participants were told only that they were helping evaluate 'a movie recommendation service'. Satisfaction and perceived diversity were measured with a validated questionnaire at the end of the session.

why: Participants unaware which algorithm served them; outcomes were self-reported and no assessor blinding is described.

state.methods: Two blinded assessors reviewed coded video recordings of each intubation attempt, recording time to intubation and first-pass success. Anaesthesia residents were randomised to use a videolaryngoscope or a direct laryngoscope on manikins.

why: Only video assessors blinded; residents obviously knew device.

state.methods: This was a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel-group trial (the investigators and the participants were unaware of treatment allocation). Following a 2-week run-in, patients were randomised to add-on pregabalin (150-600 mg/day, flexible) or placebo.

why: Investigators and participants unaware.

state.methods: Participants chose between two identical-looking bottles of a sports drink before each session, one of which contained caffeine (unknown to them). Allocation was therefore self-selected but concealed. Endurance time was recorded by a researcher who prepared the bottles.

why: Participants didn't know which bottle had caffeine; the recording researcher prepared them.

state.methods: Adults receiving invasive mechanical ventilation were randomised to a conservative (SpO2 88-92%) or liberal (SpO2 ≥ 96%) oxygen therapy target, maintained until extubation or day 28. Patients were deeply sedated for most of the intervention period. Ninety-day mortality was obtained from national registries; ventilator-free days were extracted from the ICU charting system.

why: Deep sedation might suggest patients were unaware, but the excerpt never states any blinding.

state.methods: Cages of rats (n=6 cages/group) were assigned to an enriched environment or a standard cage. Morris water maze performance was recorded by automated tracking software (ANY-maze). All analyses were performed by an investigator who was blinded to housing condition using coded animal IDs.

why: Only the analysing investigator blinded; animals not blinded participants.

state.methods: Patients with chronic rhinosinusitis were randomised to budesonide nasal irrigation or saline irrigation. Neither patients nor physicians were aware of allocation. Endoscopy scores (Lund-Kennedy) were graded by the rhinologist.

why: Patients and physicians unaware; the grading rhinologist is among the blinded physicians.

state.methods: Twelve community pharmacies were randomised to deliver the medication review service or usual care. Patients were recruited after randomisation by pharmacy staff. Adherence was assessed using the MARS-5 questionnaire administered by the pharmacists.

why: No blinding stated.

state.methods: Participants received either active or sham continuous positive airway pressure (sham: machine delivering sub-therapeutic pressure < 1 cmH2O through a mask with extra leak). Participants were naïve to CPAP and were told they would receive one of two pressure settings. Sleep technicians setting up the machines knew the setting and also scored the follow-up polysomnograms.

why: Participants blinded; technicians scoring outcomes knew.

state.methods: Job seekers registered at 40 employment offices in Flanders were randomised to intensive counselling or standard services. Employment status at 12 months was obtained from administrative social-security records by the evaluation team. Randomisation was not revealed to counsellors until the first meeting, after which it was openly known to both counsellor and client.

why: Allocation was concealed only until the first meeting; after that it was openly known to counsellors and clients and no blinded assessment is described.

state.methods: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty were randomised to a pneumatic tourniquet or no tourniquet. Patients were under spinal anaesthesia with a drape blocking view; however, patients were informed of their group after surgery. Knee range of motion and thigh pain were recorded by physiotherapists blinded to the tourniquet use, as the thigh was covered by a compression stocking in all patients.

why: Patients were informed of group; only physiotherapist assessors blinded.

state.methods: The children, their parents, and the dentists evaluating caries at 24 months were unaware of whether the fluoride varnish or a placebo varnish (identical colour and consistency) had been applied.

why: Children/parents and evaluating dentists unaware.

state.methods: Women with gestational diabetes were randomised to metformin or insulin. Neonatal outcomes were extracted from the medical records. Maternal glycaemic control was measured with HbA1c at 36 weeks. Birthweight centiles were calculated with customised charts.

why: Blinding not mentioned.

state.methods: Randomisation and masking: Randomisation was done centrally by an independent statistician using a computer-generated list with variable block sizes of 4 and 6, stratified by centre. This was an open-label trial; masking of participants and physiotherapists was not possible given the nature of the intervention (inpatient multidisciplinary rehabilitation vs outpatient physiotherapy), and outcome assessment was done by the treating team.

why: Open-label; outcome assessment by the unmasked treating team.

state.methods: Participants were randomised to psilocybin 25 mg or niacin 100 mg as an active placebo, each with preparation and integration psychotherapy. Participants and the session monitors were blinded to condition. Because psilocybin produces unmistakable subjective effects, we additionally used remote, blinded raters (connected by video, never informed of dosing session details) to administer the GRID-HAMD.

why: Participants, monitors and remote raters blinded.

state.methods: Schools were randomly allocated to deliver a 10-lesson sexual-health curriculum or to continue standard personal and social education. Pupil questionnaires were administered in classrooms by researchers. Teachers delivering lessons received two days of training.

why: No blinding statement.

state.methods: Patients with acute ankle sprain were randomised to a semi-rigid brace or a compression bandage. Patients and treating physicians could not be blinded. An independent physiotherapist, masked to treatment, assessed the Foot and Ankle Ability Measure at 4 weeks after the brace/bandage had been removed and the ankle was covered with a standard sock.

why: Only the masked independent physiotherapist was blinded.

state.methods: Subjects were blinded to the nature of the dental anaesthetic (articaine vs lidocaine), which was delivered from unmarked cartridges by the operating dentist, who knew which was which and also recorded the need for supplemental injections.

why: Subjects blinded; the recording dentist knew the drug.

state.methods: Healthy adults consumed three test breakfasts (high-fibre oats, low-fibre cereal, or no breakfast) on separate mornings in random order. Postprandial glucose was measured with continuous glucose monitors, and appetite ratings were collected with visual analogue scales at 30-minute intervals.

why: No blinding mentioned.

state.methods: We did not blind participants, treating clinicians, outcome assessors or statisticians. This pragmatic decision reflected the nature of the comparison (continuous glucose monitoring vs. finger-stick self-monitoring) and the objective primary outcome (HbA1c from the central laboratory).

why: Nobody blinded, stated explicitly.

state.methods: Stroke survivors with aphasia were randomised to intensive constraint-induced aphasia therapy or distributed standard therapy. Language outcomes (Western Aphasia Battery) were administered by speech pathologists who were blinded to treatment allocation and time point; recordings were scored by a second rater, also blinded.

why: Only the testing and scoring speech pathologists were blinded.

state.methods: Double-blind placebo-controlled trial. Patients with irritable bowel syndrome with diarrhoea received rifaximin 550 mg TID or matching placebo for 14 days.

why: Bare 'double-blind' with matching placebo, labelled participants plus investigators/assessors per the rule.

state.methods: Radiology reports were generated either by clinicians or by our report-generation model. Five board-certified radiologists graded each report for clinical errors. We did not conceal the report source from the graders, since the model reports carried a distinctive template header that could not be removed without editing content.

why: Graders explicitly not blinded to source, and there are no participants to blind, so nobody was blinded.

state.methods: Participants in the intervention arm were given an activity tracker with personalised step goals and prompts; participants in the control arm were given the same tracker showing time and steps only. To keep participants blind to allocation, they were told the study compared 'two tracker settings'. Step counts were downloaded by the research team, who configured the devices.

why: Participants blinded via the 'two settings' framing; the research team configuring devices knew.

state.methods: Participants were allocated to high-dose or low-dose influenza vaccine according to their birth month (odd vs even). Laboratory-confirmed influenza was identified from routine surveillance.

why: No blinding mentioned.

state.methods: The research assistant who administered the Montreal Cognitive Assessment at follow-up was blinded to group allocation. Participants in the intervention group attended weekly group aerobic exercise; the control group received monthly health education talks. Group leaders and participants were aware of the programme they attended.

why: Only the MoCA-administering RA was blinded.

state.methods: The allocation was open to both the participant and investigator. Participants received either a prescription for a daily 30-minute walk ('green prescription') or advice only.

why: Allocation open to participant and investigator.

state.methods: Female volunteers applied either the test moisturiser (with 5% niacinamide) or the vehicle cream to both forearms twice daily for 28 days. Jars were identical and coded. Volunteers were not told which product they had. Skin hydration was measured with a corneometer by the study technician who dispensed the jars and kept the code sheet at the measurement desk.

why: Volunteers unaware; measuring technician held the code sheet.

state.methods: Children were allocated to the reading intervention by their teachers based on perceived need. Pre- and post-test reading fluency (words correct per minute) was assessed by the school's learning support assistant.

why: No blinding statement.

state.methods: Participants and outcome assessors were masked; therapists delivering the injections were not. Participants received ultrasound-guided corticosteroid injection or ultrasound-guided saline injection into the subacromial bursa, with the ultrasound screen turned away from the patient.

why: Participants and outcome assessors masked.

state.methods: Evaluation of the primary endpoint was conducted by an independent adjudication committee blinded to treatment. Patients were randomised to a transcatheter valve or surgical aortic valve replacement; the procedures differ and are known to patients and operators.

why: Only the adjudication committee blinded.

state.methods: Open label; masking not applicable. Children with severe acute malnutrition were randomised to standard RUTF or a reduced-dose RUTF protocol. Anthropometric measurements were taken by study nurses at weekly clinic visits.

why: Open label.

state.methods: Participants were led to believe they were taking part in a study about taste perception. They were randomised to drink either a sugar-sweetened lemonade or an artificially sweetened lemonade (visually identical) before completing a self-control task (anagram persistence). The experimenter, who prepared the drinks immediately before each session, timed persistence with a stopwatch.

why: Participants couldn't tell the drinks apart; the timing experimenter prepared them and so knew.

state.methods: Patients were randomly assigned to have their inguinal hernia repaired under local or general anaesthesia. Postoperative pain, time to discharge and patient satisfaction were recorded. Blinding was not described in the original protocol.
